title: Adam Kadmon and the Anthropos
author: Ethan James Farrell
description: A custom study from Ethan's own collection, subtitled The Primordial Human as Cosmology in Jewish Mysticism and Gnostic Scripture and framed as an exploration in comparative cosmology. It takes up one figure seen through two traditions: the Kabbalists' Adam Kadmon, the primordial man of light who must be repaired, and the Gnostics' Anthropos, the heavenly human who must be remembered. After a prelude on the human being as a diagram of everything, Part One sets out the problem of the primordial human: why the universe was imagined in human shape, four ways of reading 'in our image', and cosmogony through emanation, descent and counterpart. Later parts examine Adam Kadmon in Sefer Yetzirah, the Zohar and Lurianic Kabbalah, and the Anthropos in Nag Hammadi texts, before letting the two traditions argue over creation, the fall and restoration. It is useful as a thematic bridge between the library's Kabbalah and Gnostic holdings.
